title: Path-traversal/absolute-path rejection independent of zip crate (CVE-2025-29787)
description:
Parent epic:  pptx-compose-pep7
Spec ref:     specs/011-zip-io-and-security.md#security-requirements; specs/010-opc-package-model.md#part-name-normalization

Context:
Defense-in-depth path-traversal guard. The `zip` crate had CVE-2025-29787 (a
patched traversal bug); per spec 011 and the crate-stack note we must NOT rely on
the crate alone. Every entry name passes our own rejection before its bytes are
admitted to the PartStore. Serves safety of the parse step.

Target crate / files:
- crates/pptx-compose-core/src/zip/reader.rs (edit) — gate each entry through the
  independent check before admitting it.
- crates/pptx-compose-core/src/opc/part_name.rs (edit) — expose the reusable
  traversal/absolute-path predicate used by the gate (shares logic with task xzs6's
  normalization but is asserted independently of the zip crate's own sanitization).

Change:
- `fn reject_unsafe_entry(raw_name: &str) -> Result<(), Error>` rejecting, BEFORE
  and INDEPENDENT of any `zip`-crate sanitization: absolute paths (leading `/` or
  `\`), drive/UNC forms (`C:\`, `\\host`), and any `..`/`.`-traversal segment after
  backslash-normalize + single percent-decode. Returns `Error::unsafe_path` (code
  per specs/044).
- Wire the gate into `read_entries` so a traversal entry aborts the whole open with
  `unsafe_path` (exit code per specs/071) rather than being silently skipped.

Acceptance:
`cargo test -p pptx-compose-core zip::reader::rejects_traversal` passes: a crafted
in-memory ZIP containing `../../etc/passwd` (and a `%2e%2e/` encoded variant) causes
`from_bytes` to return `Error::unsafe_path`, asserted independently of the zip crate
version.

Risks / out of scope:
Do NOT extract entries to the filesystem (spec 011: never extract to a directory by
default). Resource limits (zip-bomb) are task daxf, not here. Cleanroom: implement
the CVE defense from the spec, do NOT port TS logic.

title: Streaming resource-limit enforcement: 8 limits + 200:1 ratio -> resource_limit_exceeded/exit12
description:
Parent epic:  pptx-compose-pep7
Spec ref:     specs/011-zip-io-and-security.md#security-requirements (resource limits + zip-bomb defense)

Context:
Zip-bomb and resource-exhaustion defense. The eight configurable limits and the
200:1 per-entry ratio must abort DURING streaming inflate, before a malicious entry
can be fully decompressed. Serves safety of the parse step and the zip-bomb negative
eval (spec 081).

Target crate / files:
- crates/pptx-compose-core/src/zip/limits.rs (new) — `ResourceLimits` struct with
  the 8 V1 defaults + a streaming-aware enforcing reader wrapper.
- crates/pptx-compose-core/src/zip/reader.rs (edit) — decompress each entry through
  the limit-enforcing wrapper; accept `OpenOptions` overrides.

Change:
- `struct ResourceLimits` with the spec-011 defaults: max compressed package bytes
  524288000; max uncompressed package bytes 2147483648; max part count 10000; max
  single-part uncompressed 268435456; max media part 67108864; max per-entry ratio
  200:1; max XML depth 256; max XML node count 5000000. Overridable via OpenOptions.
- An inflating reader adapter that tracks running uncompressed bytes per entry and
  per package and the live uncompressed/compressed ratio, aborting with
  `Error::resource_limit_exceeded` (exit 12 per specs/071) the moment ANY threshold
  is crossed — never decompress fully then check.
- Part-count limit checked as entries are admitted.
- (XML depth/node-count limits are surfaced here as fields but enforced by the XML
  parser task pptx-compose-n1ux; media-size limit also exposed to task rxp1.)

Acceptance:
`cargo test -p pptx-compose-core zip::limits::aborts_zip_bomb_during_inflate` passes:
a highly-compressible entry exceeding the 200:1 ratio aborts with
`resource_limit_exceeded` after inflating only a bounded number of bytes (assert the
inflate stopped early, not after full expansion).

Risks / out of scope:
Do NOT buffer the whole decompressed entry before checking (defeats the defense). XML
depth/node enforcement is the parser's job (n1ux); this task only carries the limit
values + byte/ratio/count enforcement. Cleanroom: enforce per spec, no TS port.

title: Pre-ZIP format sniff: CFBF + EncryptionInfo/EncryptedPackage -> unsupported_package/exit11
description:
Parent epic:  pptx-compose-pep7
Spec ref:     specs/011-zip-io-and-security.md#package-format-detection-pre-zip-sniff

Context:
Encrypted/binary decks must fail with a clear, fixture-testable error instead of
crashing deep in the ZIP reader. V1 does not decrypt; a clean `unsupported_package`
is the contract that pins the encrypted-deck negative eval (spec 081). Runs at the
very front of the parse step, before any ZIP parsing.

Target crate / files:
- crates/pptx-compose-core/src/zip/reader.rs (edit) — call the sniff before opening
  the archive; OR a small `zip/sniff.rs` (new) helper invoked first.

Change:
- `fn sniff_package(head: &[u8], reader) -> Result<(), Error>` per spec 011 table:
  - leading `D0 CF 11 E0 A1 B1 1A E1` (OLE/CFBF: encrypted OOXML or legacy `.ppt`)
    -> `Error::unsupported_package` (exit 11), NO zip parse attempted.
  - leading `50 4B 03 04` whose archive contains an `EncryptionInfo` and/or
    `EncryptedPackage` stream/part -> `Error::unsupported_package` (exit 11).
  - leading `50 4B 03 04` otherwise -> Ok (proceed to OPC parse).
  - anything else -> `Error::unsupported_package` (exit 11).
- Add the `unsupported_package` error variant if not already present (code per
  specs/044; exit 11 per specs/071).

Acceptance:
`cargo test -p pptx-compose-core zip::sniff` passes: a CFBF-magic byte buffer and a
ZIP containing an `EncryptedPackage` entry both yield `Error::unsupported_package`;
fixtures/minimal.pptx passes the sniff and proceeds.

Risks / out of scope:
Do NOT attempt decryption or CFBF parsing — opaque rejection only. Do NOT consume the
reader such that a valid package can no longer be read (peek/rewind the header).
Cleanroom: detect per the spec table, not via any TS heuristic.

title: ZIP writer raw_copy_file passthrough for clean parts; preserve entry order
description:
Parent epic:  pptx-compose-pep7
Spec ref:     specs/011-zip-io-and-security.md#preservation-requirements; specs/020-xml-handling.md (clean = raw passthrough)

Context:
The write side of lossless I/O. Clean (unmodified) parts must be written back
byte-for-byte without re-compression or re-serialization, which is what makes the
no-edit round trip byte-identical (spec 050). Serves the write step of the workflow.

Target crate / files:
- crates/pptx-compose-core/src/zip/writer.rs (new) — ZIP writer over the `zip`
  crate using `ZipWriter::raw_copy_file` for clean parts.

Change:
- `fn write_clean(&mut writer, entry: &RawEntry)` calls `ZipWriter::raw_copy_file`
  (zip 8.6.x) to copy the stored compressed stream + CRC + metadata verbatim — no
  inflate/deflate cycle — for any part whose dirty flag is false (dirty-tracking is
  task pptx-compose-x46t).
- `fn write_dirty(&mut writer, name, bytes, meta)` re-adds modified parts with the
  active compression profile.
- Preserve original ZIP entry ORDER from ZipEntryMetadata when in preserve mode.
- Output forms `write_vec() -> Vec<u8>` and `write_writer(Write+Seek)` per spec 011
  Output Forms.

Acceptance:
`cargo test -p pptx-compose-core zip::writer::raw_copy_is_byte_identical` passes:
reading fixtures/minimal.pptx then writing every entry via write_clean yields a byte
stream whose per-entry stored bytes and entry order are identical to the input.

Risks / out of scope:
Do NOT re-serialize or re-compress clean parts (that would break byte identity).
Determinism normalization (stable timestamps/order for dirty output) is task 134t.
Dirty-tracking logic lives in task x46t; this task only honors a passed-in dirty flag.
Cleanroom: do NOT port any TS zip-writing path.

title: ZIP reader: entries, raw uncompressed bytes, ZipEntryMetadata
description:
Parent epic:  pptx-compose-pep7
Spec ref:     specs/011-zip-io-and-security.md#input-forms (preservation reqs); specs/010-opc-package-model.md#part-names

Context:
The read side of lossless package I/O. Reads a ZIP container into raw, uncompressed
part bytes plus the per-entry metadata needed to reproduce the archive faithfully
on write. This is the entry point of the parse step and the source of the bytes the
round-trip invariants (spec 050) protect.

Target crate / files:
- crates/pptx-compose-core/src/zip/reader.rs (new) — ZIP reader over the `zip`
  crate (8.6.x); yields entries as (PartName, raw bytes, ZipEntryMetadata).
- crates/pptx-compose-core/src/zip/mod.rs (new) — `ZipEntryMetadata` struct +
  module wiring.

Change:
- `struct ZipEntryMetadata { original_name: String, compression_method, crc32,
  compressed_size, uncompressed_size, last_modified, external_attrs, is_dir }` —
  enough to round-trip entry order and compression choices in preserve mode.
- `fn read_entries(reader: impl Read + Seek) -> Result<Vec<RawEntry>>` where
  `RawEntry { name: PartName, bytes: Vec<u8>, meta: ZipEntryMetadata }`; preserves
  original entry ORDER (spec 011 preservation: "Preserve original part ordering").
- Each entry name is normalized via `PartName::from_zip_entry` (task xzs6); directory
  entries are retained as metadata, not as content parts.
- Returns raw UNCOMPRESSED bytes per entry (no XML parsing here — boundary rule).
- Provides `from_bytes(&[u8])` and `open_reader(Read+Seek)` entry points per spec 011
  Input Forms.

Acceptance:
`cargo test -p pptx-compose-core zip::reader::reads_minimal_pptx` passes: opening
fixtures/minimal.pptx yields N entries whose PartNames and raw byte lengths match the
known fixture, in original archive order, with ZipEntryMetadata populated.

Risks / out of scope:
Do NOT enforce resource limits here (task daxf wires limits into streaming inflate)
and do NOT sniff format here (task dpry). Do NOT parse or re-encode XML. Do NOT rely
on the `zip` crate alone for path safety (CVE-2025-29787 — task 0nug). Cleanroom:
build to spec, not to any TS unzip path.

title: PartStore + canonical PartName (normalize, reject dup/traversal, case-sensitive segments)
description:
Parent epic:  pptx-compose-pep7
Spec ref:     specs/010-opc-package-model.md#part-name-normalization (also #part-names, #package-invariants)

Context:
Foundation of the OPC layer used by parse and write. Every ZIP entry name is
turned into a canonical PartName that is the identity key for parts, relationship
resolution, and content-type lookup. Must reject unsafe/duplicate names so no
later layer can be fooled into traversal or part-aliasing. Serves the parse step
of input.pptx -> OPC package.

Target crate / files:
- crates/pptx-compose-core/src/opc/part_name.rs (new) — PartName newtype + the
  exact 5-step normalization procedure from spec 010.
- crates/pptx-compose-core/src/opc/part.rs (new) — PartStore: insert/lookup by
  PartName, rejecting collisions; retains original ZIP entry name for byte-faithful
  write.
- crates/pptx-compose-core/src/error/mod.rs (edit) — add `unsafe_path` and
  `duplicate_part` error variants (codes per specs/044).

Change:
- `struct PartName(String)` holding canonical form (exactly one leading `/`,
  forward slashes, percent-decoded once, no empty/`.`/`..` segments, no trailing
  slash, no drive/UNC). `PartName::from_zip_entry(&str) -> Result<PartName, Error>`
  implements spec 010 steps 1-5 verbatim; any failing step returns
  `Error::unsafe_path`. Segment comparison is case-SENSITIVE (no lowercasing).
- `PartName::zip_entry_name(&self) -> &str` returns the no-leading-slash form for
  the ZIP writer; original authored entry name is stored alongside for fidelity.
- `struct PartStore` keyed by PartName; `insert` returns `Error::duplicate_part`
  when two ZIP entries normalize to the same PartName. `get(&PartName) -> Option<&Part>`,
  `get_mut`, ordered iteration preserving insertion order.
- No PowerPoint knowledge in this module (boundary rule, spec 060).

Acceptance:
`cargo test -p pptx-compose-core opc::part_name` passes, covering: `/ppt/slides/slide1.xml`
accepted; `../evil.xml`, `/ppt/../evil.xml`, `a//b`, trailing-slash, and `C:\x`
rejected with `unsafe_path`; `/ppt/Slides/x.xml` vs `/ppt/slides/x.xml` are distinct
keys; two entries normalizing equal -> `duplicate_part`.

Risks / out of scope:
Do NOT lowercase part names (only content-type Default-extension match is
case-insensitive, spec 012 — not here). Do NOT resolve relationship targets here
(that is spec 010 #relative-target-resolution, task pptx-compose-21uo). Cleanroom:
implement the spec procedure, do NOT port any TS path handling.

title: Deterministic write mode: stable order/timestamps/compression, no clean re-serialize
description:
Parent epic:  pptx-compose-pep7
Spec ref:     specs/011-zip-io-and-security.md#deterministic-output; specs/070-public-api-and-cli.md (write options)

Context:
Deterministic write mode gives stable, testable output for golden tests without
re-serializing clean parts. Clean parts still pass through raw (task he9h); this task
only normalizes the archive-level variables (order, timestamps, compression) so two
runs produce identical bytes. Serves the write step and the golden round-trip tests
(spec 050, task k438).

Target crate / files:
- crates/pptx-compose-core/src/zip/writer.rs (edit) — add a `WriteMode`/`WriteOptions`
  switch (Preserve vs Deterministic) controlling entry order, timestamps, compression.

Change:
- `enum WriteMode { Preserve, Deterministic }` on `WriteOptions`.
- Deterministic mode: stable ZIP entry order (preserve original order when available,
  else a defined canonical order), normalized/fixed last-modified timestamps, fixed
  compression settings, and stable content-type/relationship ordering — per spec 011
  "Deterministic Output" bullets.
- Clean parts are STILL emitted via raw_copy_file (task he9h); deterministic mode
  must NOT trigger a re-serialize of clean parts. Only dirty parts are re-encoded,
  with the fixed compression profile.
- Document that whole-file byte equality across modes is not promised; determinism is
  guaranteed run-to-run within Deterministic mode (spec 011).

Acceptance:
`cargo test -p pptx-compose-core zip::writer::deterministic_is_stable_cross_run`
passes: writing the same Package twice in Deterministic mode yields byte-identical
output, and clean parts are confirmed to have gone through raw_copy_file (not
re-serialized).

Risks / out of scope:
Do NOT re-serialize or re-order clean part BYTES (only archive-level metadata is
normalized). Dirty-tracking is task x46t; XML canonical-write profile for dirty parts
is task xh1f. Cleanroom: follow spec 011 determinism rules, no TS port.
